title: The Crooked Crown
premise: Wendell Galloway, a memory-thief and reluctant bookkeeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, is tasked with cataloguing a child who arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom. The child's words are fragments of King Aldric's true self, sealed away when the usurper Veyra bound him to the Crooked Crown, an artifact that devours identity to fuel her armies. Wendell discovers their own stolen memories contain the ritual needed to unbind the king — memories they sold long ago to survive. As Veyra's legions march on the free cities, Wendell must choose between reclaiming the self they sold and using that sacrifice to free Aldric. In the end, Wendell gives up their recovered past entirely: the king is unbound, Veyra's crown crumbles, and Wendell survives as someone new — nameless, but finally whole.
about_author: Rafael Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated manuscripts in a coastal city's customs house before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ledgers, thieves, and the terrible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A night of routine guild work goes wrong when a silent child is left at the door, speaking a language no living scholar knows. Wendell, whose trade is stealing and storing memories, recognizes the cadence from a memory they sold years ago. The beat is unease — the past knocking at a door Wendell thought locked.

chapters.title: What the Child Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The guild's mistress orders the child contained; Wendell secretly records the child's speech and matches it to fragments in their own ledger of stolen memories. The words describe a king being unmade by his own crown. The beat is dawning dread: Wendell sold something vital once, and it mattered.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: POV Wendell in flashback interwoven with present. We learn how Wendell sold their childhood memories to the guild to buy food during the famine years — including, unknowingly, knowledge of the Unbinding Rite learned from a dying court mage. The beat is grief for a self deliberately discarded.

chapters.title: Veyra's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wendell and a deserter soldier, Brannoc, who arrives wounded with news: Queen-regent Veyra's armies have taken two river cities, and she hunts 'a vessel of the old tongue.' The child is the last living fragment of King Aldric. The beat is the world closing in — flight becomes inevitable.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Ashvale
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell steals the child and flees with Brannoc through burned farmland toward the mountain shrine where the rite must be performed. Veyra's hunters, the Hollowed — soldiers with their faces smoothed blank — track them. The beat is fragile found-family forming under pursuit.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Salt Market
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. In the free city of Casterhale, Wendell bargains with a memory-broker to glimpse what they sold — and sees themselves as a child, happy, and hates what survival cost. The broker offers the full memory back at a cruel price: another year of Wendell's future. The beat is temptation and refusal.

chapters.title: The Hollowed Close In
chapters.summary: POV Brannoc. Ambushed on the shrine road, Brannoc holds a bridge against the Hollowed so Wendell and the child can escape; he falls, though not certainly dead. The child speaks its first word in common tongue: Wendell's name. The beat is sacrifice and the terrifying intimacy of being remembered.

chapters.title: The Shrine of the First Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. At the shrine, the rite requires a speaker of the old tongue who willingly surrenders their own memories as kindling. Wendell realizes the child cannot survive the rite — but Wendell's sold memories, held in the guild vaults, can be used instead. The beat is resolve hardening into plan.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell breaks into the guild vault, reclaims their stolen memories, and performs the rite as Veyra arrives with her army. The memories burn; the Crooked Crown shatters; Aldric rises whole while Veyra, severed from her artifact, collapses into nothing. The beat is climax — total loss and total victory in one breath.

chapters.title: Someone New
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. With the war ended, King Aldric offers Wendell anything; Wendell asks only for work and a name of their own choosing. Standing before the guild ledger, now empty, Wendell writes a first entry in a fresh book. The beat is quiet resolution: identity rebuilt not from the past, but chosen forward.
